newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Wednesday's European Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Wednesday's European Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Wednesday:

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said the Commission had decided to postpone to December 18 decisions on the common organisation of the tobacco market and on the future role of the Community in the fight against tobacco consumption. The Commission juged necessary to deepen the reflection on the socio-economic consequences of such decisions, he said.
Vale de Almeida said DG1 Director Herve Jouanjean would hold a news conference at 1215/1115 GMT on Thursday on EU priorities before the World Trade Organisation's ministerial conference in Singapore.

Vale de Almeida announced a joint news conference by Commission President Jacques Santer and Irish Prime Minister and European Council President John Bruton at 1430/1330 GMT on Thursday Brutons' tour of EU capitals ahead of Dublin's European Council.
He also announced that President Santer and Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi would hold a news conference in the Breydel's VIP corner at 1715/1615 GMT on Thursday.
Vale de Almeida announced the birth of spokeswoman Sarah Lambert's daughter Gabriella who weights 2.5 kilos.

Vale de Almeida said the Commission had nominated new European Commission Directors General. He said Colette Flesch would lead the translation services and the information technology directorate, that Steffen Smidt would lead DGIX and that Michel Vanden Abeele would lead DGXXIII.

In answer to a question spokesman Willy Helin said he had not received any information that French authorities had abandoned the idea of privatising Thomson SA. He also said that even if the French authorities had done so or if they had changed their minds about future buyers, the regulation obliged the Commission to take a decision on a case that was submitted to them.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/1107: Member states reject proposed ban on beef and sheep tissues.
- IP/96/1116: Strategic environmental assessment: the Commission proposes to strengthen the system.
- IP/96/1117: Following an undertaking by AC Nielsen to change its contractual practices, the Commission suspends its action for breach of competition rules.
- IP/96/1118: Commission report to European Council confirms the mutually beneficial effects of greater co-ordination of economic and structural policies.
- IP/96/1119: Republics of former Yugoslavia: European Commission earmarks ECU 85 million for refugees, displaced people and vulnerable groups.
- IP/96/1120: Commission opposes creation of joint venture between Saint-Gobain, Wacker-Chemie and NOM.
- IP/96/1122: The European Commission proposes a voluntary service programme.
- IP/96/1123: Commission proposes European space strategy.
- IP/96/1124: Commission fines Systemform GmbH ECU 100,000.
- IP/96/1125: EC-Pakistan new cooperation agreement negotiations.
- IP/96/1126: State aid: France - Island of Reunion: Commission gives green light to aid for ECOPIPE.
- IP/96/1127: Commission forbids application of Maribel II and III (Belgium).
- IP/96/1128: Commission declares DM 30 million aid to Bestwood illegal.
- IP/96/1129: Commission approves new Swedish fiscal measures concerning CO2.
- IP/96/1130: Commission approves the Danish fiscal package on waste water tax.
- IP/96/1131: Commission approves transport aid to Finnish regions.
- Speech/96/317: Extracts from speech by Commissioner Mario Monti to the Bundestag Committee of Finance.
- Speech/96/318: Opening statement by Commissioner Franz Fischler to the European Parliament's Committee of Inquiry into BSE.
- Oil Bulletin No 847.
- ME96/4.12: Midday express.
